title: In my opinion

fn.en: Ask for and give opinions; write for social media.

gr: the language of asking for and giving an opinion

can.en: I can ask for and give an opinion, and write a short post that gives one.

rc: state verbs and the present tenses

acts.say: Read each phrase out loud before you sort it.

items.x: If you ask me, it won’t work.
Don’t you think it’s too expensive?
How do you feel about it?
As far as I’m concerned, it’s finished.

items.r: a series of connected posts by the same person
the short text written under a photo
somebody who chooses to see everything you post
a word with # in front of it that groups posts together
a chance to do something you want to do
something good that you managed to do

items.q: The film had a deep ___ on the way I think.
“If you ask me” is a useful ___ for giving your view.
Nobody has the ___ to change this on their own.
Passing the exam at sixteen was a real ___.
The ___ has promised a decision before the summer.
He is a full-time speaker on the psychology of ___.
The dictionary ___ of “friend” is much wider than it used to be.
Making that ___ was harder than I expected.
Nobody read it, so I removed the ___ to the article.
Please don’t ___ that photo — I look terrible in it.
She left a long ___ under my post disagreeing with all of it.
The new law had a strong ___ on small shops.
Learning a language is a slow ___, not a single event.
The film affected me ___ — I thought about it for weeks.

sub.en: All of these give an opinion. Choose the one that fits the situation.

items.q: You are writing a formal essay. Which opening is right?
o: In my opinion, the evidence is weak.
If you ask me, the evidence is rubbish.
Nah, the evidence is weak.
items.why: In my opinion is neutral and works in formal writing; If you ask me is informal and spoken.

items.q: A friend asks what you think about her new job offer. Which is most natural?
o: I’d say take it.
It is my opinion that you should take it.
In accordance with my view, take it.

items.q: You want somebody to tell you their view.
o: What do you reckon?
What do you reckon me?
What are you reckoning?
items.why: reckon = think. It is informal and, like think, it is a state verb.

items.q: You agree with somebody completely.
o: I couldn’t agree more.
I couldn’t agree anymore.
I couldn’t be more agree.

items.q: You want to disagree, but politely.
o: I see your point, but…
You are wrong, but…
I don’t agree you, but…

items.q: You are giving your view in a work email.
o: As far as I’m concerned, the deadline is unrealistic.
As far as I concern, the deadline is unrealistic.
As far I’m concerned, the deadline is unrealistic.

acts.title: Three posts, one opinion
parts: 3 · a question back to the reader
text: In my opinion the ban on plastic bags in our supermarkets has been a real achievement. Six months in, the shops are cleaner, the river is cleaner, and nobody has died of carrying a bag from home.

If you ask me, the interesting part isn’t the ban itself — it’s how fast people changed. We were told it would take years. It took about three weeks. That says something about our ability to adapt, and I find it deeply encouraging.
I’d say the next choice is harder: coffee cups. I don’t think a small charge will be enough this time. What do you reckon? Reply below — I read every comment.

items.r: picks out what the writer finds most interesting
asks the readers for their view
helps people who care about the topic find the post

items.q: Find the three-word phrase the writer uses to open her opinion. (In m… o…)
Find the four-word informal phrase that opens post 2. (If y… a… me)
Find the two words the writer uses to give a careful opinion. (I’d …)
Find the four-word question she uses to ask her readers. (What d… y… r…?)
Find the phrase she uses to disagree with an idea in advance. (I d… t…)

acts.genre: Register · the same opinion, two places
acts.title: Post or essay?
text: A social-media post is short, personal and speaks directly to the reader. Contractions, dashes and questions are normal.
A formal essay keeps the writer in the background. No contractions, no direct questions to the reader, and the evidence comes before the opinion.

items.x: If you ask me, it’s already working.
The evidence suggests that the policy has been effective.
What do you reckon? Reply below.
It could therefore be argued that a charge is insufficient.
Six months in, and the river is cleaner.
In conclusion, the ban represents a significant achievement.

lines: In my opinion, this campaign [is working|works|has worked] right now — look at the streets.
I [don’t think|am not thinking|haven’t thought] the government [understands|is understanding|has understood] the problem.
As far as I’m concerned, the process [has already begun|already begins|is already beginning to begin].
I [reckon|am reckoning|have reckoned] most of my followers [agree|are agreeing|have agreed] with me.
She [has posted|posts|is posting] three threads about it this week, and people [are sharing|share|have shared] them everywhere.

items.why: In my opinion is followed directly by the clause: In my opinion the ban is working.
think = have an opinion is a state, so the simple form is used.
agree is a verb: I don’t agree. Not I am not agree.
I couldn’t agree more = I agree completely. anymore has a different meaning.
have = possess is a state, so the simple form is used.

items.from: I am not sure that is right.
items.cue: Rewrite it as a polite disagreement with SO SURE.
items.a: I’m not so sure about that
alt: I am not so sure about that

tts: So, Jem, what do you think about the idea?
Well, as far as I’m concerned, anything which makes people think more about what they are buying is a good idea.
There’s a lot more awareness now, but don’t you think it would be better if people simply bought less?
I’m convinced that if people really understood the damage, they wouldn’t keep replacing their phones.
Well, according to the people who make it, the phone will last longer and is easier to repair.
If you ask me, we have to give people the option of buying something better for the planet.

items.s: So, what do you think about the idea?
As far as I’m concerned, anything which makes people think is a good idea.
But don’t you think it would be better if people simply bought less?
I’m convinced that if people really understood the damage, they wouldn’t do it.
Well, according to the people who make it, it will last longer.
If you ask me, we have to give people the option.

items.sit: You are writing a comment under a serious news article and you want to sound measured.
o: In my opinion the report leaves out the cost.
If you ask me the report is rubbish.
Nah, the report’s wrong.

items.sit: A friend has just said exactly what you were thinking.
o: I couldn’t agree more.
I couldn’t agree anymore.
I am agreeing more.

items.sit: You want your followers to reply to your post.
o: What do you reckon? Reply below.
What are you reckoning? Reply below.
What do you reckon about? Reply below.

items.sit: Somebody makes a fair point that you still disagree with.
o: I see your point, but I still think it’s too expensive.
You are wrong, but it’s too expensive.
I see your point, but I am still thinking it’s too expensive.

items.sit: You are giving a careful, not-too-strong opinion in a meeting.
o: I’d say we need another week.
I’d saying we need another week.
I’d say to need another week.

items.sit: You are asked whether the new rule will work, and you are doubtful.
o: I don’t think it will be enough.
I am not thinking it will be enough.
I don’t think it will be enough, isn’t it?

write.q: Write your own thread of three short posts giving an opinion on something in your city — transport, prices, a new building, a rule. Follow the model: post 1 = the opinion and the evidence, post 2 = what you find most interesting, post 3 = a question to your readers. Add two hashtags.
write.model:
In my opinion the new bus lane on Bukhar Zhyrau has been a real improvement. Six weeks in, my journey to work has dropped from forty minutes to twenty-five. #karaganda #transport

If you ask me, the interesting part isn’t the buses — it’s that half the drivers I know have stopped complaining. Nobody expected that.

I’d say the next choice is harder: parking in the centre. I don’t think a small fine will be enough. What do you reckon? Reply below — I read every comment.

speak.q: Say your opinion out loud, as if you were speaking to a friend and not writing. Give the opinion, one reason, and one piece of evidence, then ask for their view.
speak.model: If you ask me, the new bus lane has made a real difference. My journey to work used to take forty minutes; now it takes twenty-five. And the interesting part is that people who complained about it have gone quiet. I’d say parking is the next problem, but I don’t think a small fine will change anything. What do you reckon?
